sections.title: Memory and recall
sections.content:
Words for how we remember and forget:
• recollect — remember something. I can't recollect where I put my keys.
• reminisce — think about pleasant past experiences. They spent the evening reminiscing about university days.
• retain — keep in memory. Students retain information better with active learning.
• slip one's mind — forget temporarily. I'm sorry, the meeting completely slipped my mind.
• memorise — learn by heart. She memorised the entire speech overnight.

sections.title: Intelligence and thinking
sections.content:
Describing mental abilities:
• perceptive — quick to notice and understand. She's extremely perceptive about people's emotions.
• intuitive — understanding without conscious reasoning. He has an intuitive grasp of complex systems.
• analytical — using logical reasoning. Analytical thinking is essential for problem-solving.
• innate — inborn, natural. She has an innate talent for languages.
• cognitive — relating to mental processes. Cognitive skills decline without regular mental exercise.

exercises.question: To think fondly about past experiences is to:
exercises.explanation: Reminisce means to indulge in enjoyable recollection of past events.

exercises.question: Understanding something without conscious reasoning is:
exercises.explanation: Intuitive means using or based on what one feels to be true without conscious reasoning.

exercises.question: When you forget something temporarily, it:
exercises.explanation: Slips one's mind means to be temporarily forgotten.

exercises.question: A natural talent you're born with is:
exercises.hint: You didn't learn it — you were born with it.

exercises.question: Thinking that uses logic and careful examination is:
exercises.explanation: Analytical means relating to or using analysis or logical reasoning.

exercises.question: To keep information in your memory is to:
exercises.explanation: Retain means to continue to have; to keep in memory.

exercises.question: Relating to mental processes like thinking and learning is:
exercises.explanation: Cognitive relates to the mental processes of perception, memory, and reasoning.

exercises.question: Someone who quickly notices subtle things is:
exercises.explanation: Perceptive means having a keen insight and understanding.
